summary: Substrate/gate-integrity fix. ci/checks/db/cross_tenant.test.ts was red on dev (`seedRowForTable: unknown table user_pref`) because migration 129 (T-0651) added choros.user_pref but the test's exhaustive per-table seeder switch had no case for it. Added a standalone seed case for user_pref (no FK deps, same pattern as the existing 'section' case: uuid() id, generic actor='seed-actor'/key='seed.key'/value='{}'::jsonb, created_at/updated_at=0) plus the required entry in the SEEDED_TABLES static-guard set (AC-CT-4 checks both the switch case AND this set independently). No product code, no schema/RLS changes — test-fixture-only.

Confirmed by name: 'AC-1 ... table: user_pref' PASS, 'AC-2 ... table: user_pref' PASS, 'AC-CT-4 ... table user_pref has a seeder in seedRowForTable' PASS.
ci_local_detail.fitness: anti-case-lock.sh (D-064 gate) — PASS, aggregate literal counts unchanged/decreased vs baseline, no case-content added (test-fixture-only change, no literals touched).

user_pref_isolation_result.isolation_verdict: PASS — user_pref IS correctly tenant-isolated. AC-1 (explicit WHERE tenant_id=B from tenant-A context -> 0 rows) and AC-2 (no WHERE, only tenant-A rows visible) both green for user_pref, proving migration 129's RLS FORCE + default-DENY policy (choros.tenant_id GUC) works as designed. Not a defect in T-0651 — the gap was purely the test's seeder coverage, not the table's security posture.

friction_events: Two places needed the new table, not one: the switch-case in seedRowForTable AND the separate SEEDED_TABLES Set used by the static AC-CT-4 completeness guard (describe block at the end of the file). Missed the second on first pass — the guard test 'table user_pref has a seeder in seedRowForTable' failed even after the switch case was added, since SEEDED_TABLES is checked independently as a belt-and-suspenders anti-drift mechanism. Fixed by adding 'user_pref' to SEEDED_TABLES; full 199/199 green on the next run.
